claim: On 4x RTX 4090 with all 12 GPU pairs reporting P2P DISABLED, FSDP SHARD_GRAD_OP (the ZeRO-2-equivalent sharding mode) runs at 4.13 samples/s versus DDP's 6.90, a 1.67x step-time ratio (+67% overhead) that exceeds cc-3's 50% overturn threshold.
stance_target: cc-3's concern that ZeRO-2's byte-volume identity with DDP does not imply wall-clock parity on a host-staged fabric
scope_conditions: 4x RTX 4090 24GB, PCIe 4.0 x16, topology PHB/NODE, P2P disabled, batch 1/GPU; model and sequence length NOT stated
quoted_support: FSDP Comparison | Strategy | Samples/sec | Memory/GPU | Forward | Backward | Optimizer | DDP 6.90 21.1 GB 0.033s 0.423s 0.128s | SHARD_GRAD_OP 4.13 15.8 GB 0.323s 0.643s 0.009s

claim: The same FSDP table shows SHARD_GRAD_OP's forward pass is 10x slower than DDP's (0.323 s vs 0.033 s) at batch 1/GPU, which identifies the regime as small-model all-gather-latency-dominated rather than a 1B/32k compute-dominated step.
stance_target: Reading the 1.67x ratio as a valid estimate of ZeRO-2 overhead at >=1B params / 32k
scope_conditions: batch 1/GPU, 4 ranks, no sequence length stated

claim: The harness confirms the fabric is host-staged and asymmetric: GPU0->GPU1 measured 247 ms / 32 Gbps while GPU1->GPU0 measured 76 ms / 105 Gbps, and a cross-NUMA pair measured 233 ms / 34 Gbps, against an expected ~200 Gbps with P2P.
stance_target: The premise that every inter-GPU byte on this class of box crosses the host bridge twice
quoted_support: GPU 0 -> GPU 1: 247ms, 32 Gbps (expected: ~200 Gbps with P2P) / GPU 1 -> GPU 0: 76ms, 105 Gbps (asymmetric!) / GPU 0 -> GPU 2: 233ms, 34 Gbps (cross-NUMA)

claim: A separate 'bad topology' DDP run on the same 4090 class shows 2 GPUs delivering 0.29x and 4 GPUs 0.91x of single-GPU throughput, i.e. DDP itself can lose more than half its throughput on a badly-wired PCIe host.
stance_target: The claim that DDP is unconditionally the safe topology on this fabric
scope_conditions: Vast.ai RTX 4090, batch 2, sdpa attention, rtx_4090_bad_topology.csv
